origin: The finding gate presented a call Claude had already made as a y-or-skip stop over an approved auto gate, because the shape came from the finding's category rather than the move it owed. This pins the contract that replaced it: a settled call rides auto with no stop, and a choice stops anyway — auto means don't pause me for what you can decide, never decide what you can't.
conduct: The user is resuming their card-payments specification to run its review; construction finished last sitting, so offered the resume choice they continue. At the first finding — the missing 30-day refund window — they see the discussion already decided it and say so: they choose auto, because they do not want to be stopped again for things the record has already settled. When the second refund detail lands without asking them, that is what they wanted. The third finding is different and they treat it differently: nothing decided how long a failed webhook keeps retrying, and both ways cost something real. They reject the recommendation — three attempts is too few for a bank having a bad morning, and they would rather hold state for a day than lose orders — and pick the 24-hour reconciliation option instead. With auto set, the follow-up review cycle runs without asking them and comes back clean, and the session moves to completion on its own; at sign-off they confirm. Throughout they answer concretely and never reopen decided questions.
